verified.name: The Big Fig

location.address: Station Street road reserve, Miriam Vale, Gladstone Region, Queensland
location.neighbourhood: Miriam Vale town centre, beside the railway station

verified.access: Free. Stands in an unused corner of the public Station Street road reserve, in the open commercial centre of Miriam Vale next to the railway station and opposite the War Memorial Park; no fence or gate, visible and reachable from both Station Street and Blomfield Street.
verified.transport: Miriam Vale town centre, on the Bruce Highway route between Gladstone and Agnes Water/Town of Seventeen Seventy; roadside in the town, no public transport needed
verified.verify_notes: Queensland Heritage Register #602323, listed 6 Jan 2004; its own 'significant period' field records 1897-c.1900, though a 1916 Bundaberg Mail article on the Miriam Vale Progress Association offers a rival planting story, so the tree is somewhere between about 110 and 130 years old and the register's own dating is used as the primary basis. Likely planted as part of a Queensland Railways station-beautification scheme (several other North Coast Line stations between Bundaberg and Gladstone received a single large Ficus benjamina at the same period), though QHR says this is unconfirmed. Trunk circumference approximately 12m (1200cm) per the QHR's own description reproduced on Wikipedia; this is a full-girth trunk figure from a mature weeping fig with buttressing and surface roots rather than a slim single stem, so treat as a trunk/buttress-mass figure. Canopy spans 30m east-west by 35m north-south, crown height 10-15m. Long civic history: milk and cream collection point until 1977 (loading ramp remnants survive as earth mounds), Anzac Day shelter since the 1921 war memorial, informal veterinary consultations in the 1950s/60s. Now the official logo of Miriam Vale Community Development Inc, which has planned (not yet built, per the QHR text) a boardwalk and interpretive signage beneath it. Alive and actively managed as of the most recent explicit confirmation found: a January 2015 Bundaberg News Mail article on Gladstone Regional Council commissioning arborist-advised root trimming and a root barrier to protect the road and neighbouring property, i.e. the council maintains it as a living asset. No death report found in any source; no confirmation newer than 2015 found either, hence flagged rather than clean-confirmed on the 'alive now' test. Explicitly called out in its own heritage listing as recognised by travellers passing through Miriam Vale to the coastal towns of Agnes Water and Town of Seventeen Seventy, i.e. it already functions as a real, if modest, waypoint destination rather than a name on a register nobody visits.
verified.destination_test: PASS, cautiously: a physically enormous, single-trunk fig (12m circumference, 30-35m canopy) that is the town's own chosen emblem, sits in the open street with no barrier, and is already a known rest stop for travellers on the coastal route rather than an obscure register entry. Demand is low (24 reads/month, the batch's weakest signal) and there is no dedicated visitor infrastructure yet beyond the tree itself, so this is a modest single-tree place rather than a headline attraction, but the scale and civic identity clear the bar the marked/blazed trees in this batch do not: there is a real, large, freely reachable thing to stand in front of.

blocked.name: Kidman's Tree of Knowledge
blocked.verify_notes: Coolibah (Eucalyptus coolibah) at Glengyle Station, Bedourie, Shire of Diamantina, Queensland, ~60km south of Bedourie on the western bank of Eyre Creek. Reputedly where Sir Sidney Kidman camped while contemplating his pastoral empire (Wikipedia itself calls the connection unproven). Queensland Heritage Register #600462, listed 1992. Described as healthy and mature, standing in a grassed square formed by the homestead and its outbuildings. BLOCKED: sits inside the working homestead compound of Glengyle Station, a private pastoral property still run by S Kidman and Company; no evidence of any public access, visitor path or invitation. Fails hard rule 10 (private working station, not genuinely open to visitors) and fails the single-tree-destination test as a result: nobody can simply travel there, it is deep in a remote station's home paddock 60km from the nearest town. Not a case of inconvenience (a gate that might be shut) but of no public access existing at all.

blocked.name: Hoop Pines, Bald Hills
blocked.verify_notes: A pair of hoop pines (Araucaria cunninghamii), the taller c.200 years old, the smaller 150+ years, at 34 Strathpine Road, Bald Hills, Brisbane. Queensland Heritage Register, listed 22 Feb 2002, connected to the Stewart/Duncan families, the district's earliest non-indigenous settlers. Also known as 'Hoop Pines at St Paul's Anglican School': the trees stand on the grounds of a currently operating school. BLOCKED: no source found stating the school grounds are open to the public (no public path crossing them, no bordering public park, no stated open hours); per the schools exception in hard rule 10 a school site ships only with real evidence of genuine public access, and none exists here. 17.4km from Brisbane, which we already publish, so this would have belonged to Brisbane rather than being its own place, but the access question blocks it regardless of container. Also a pair rather than one tree, which would need the compact-ensemble test, moot given the access block.
blocked.reason: school grounds, no evidence of public access (hard rule 10)

blocked.name: Landsborough Tree
blocked.verify_notes: Heritage-listed tree at Burketown, Shire of Burke, Queensland (Qld Heritage Register #600374, listed 21 Aug 1992), marking the northernmost depot of William Landsborough's 1862 expedition searching for Burke and Wills. BLOCKED: DEAD. Wikipedia states plainly the tree was destroyed by vandals in December 2002 and only a burnt stump remains; the heritage listing name itself is now 'Landsborough Tree (site of)'. The Burke Shire Council's own page describes the tree in the past/photo-caption tense with no confirmation of current life. A carcass or stump is never a collectible entry per the never-dead rule, however historically significant.
blocked.reason: dead: destroyed by vandals Dec 2002, burnt stump only

blocked.name: William Wyndham's gravesite (remnant orchard trees)
blocked.verify_notes: Queensland Heritage Register entry (#601811, listed 23 June 2000) for Wyndham's grave at Boyne Island, Gladstone Region, plus remnants of his 19th-century orchard 'Carnym'. The heritage listing itself covers nine mango trees and two tamarind trees scattered 'throughout the suburb' of Boyne Island; only two tamarind trees stand together, in a corner of Wyndham Park near Olunda Street (23.9369S 151.3536E). BLOCKED: not a single collectible point. The register entry is a diffuse remnant orchard spread across a whole suburb, not one tree or a compact ensemble with one obvious place to stand; even the two park tamarinds are one small piece of an eleven-tree scatter that the heritage listing treats as one entity. Per the avenue/whole-wood exclusion in the never-cuttable rules.
blocked.reason: not a single collectible point: remnant orchard trees scattered across a whole suburb

blocked.name: Moonah Creek Hanging Tree
blocked.verify_notes: Ghost Gum (Corymbia papuana) on Oban Holding, Ardmore Station, Shire of Boulia, remote north-west Queensland, near Moonah Creek and the Urandangi-Mount Isa road. Qld Heritage Register #600040, listed 2005, also called Killing Tree/Butchering Tree; oral history from the Waluwara people holds that police hanged 15 Aboriginal men here around 1900 in reprisal for cattle spearing (no documentary confirmation exists, per Wikipedia). BLOCKED, two independent reasons. (1) Alive-now check fails: Wikipedia's own account of a 2003 condition assessment states the tree 'is no longer living', describing two of four major limbs lost, the limb that held the hanging beam fallen, the beam itself missing, and bad termite damage with a large crack in the trunk; no photo or source after 2003 was found to contradict this, so the strongest available evidence says dead. (2) It sits on Oban Holding, private pastoral station land, with no visitor infrastructure or public-access path documented anywhere found. Never delivered per the hard rule that a tree known to be dead is never a collectible entry, whatever its historical weight.
blocked.reason: dead per 2003 assessment (no longer living, termite damage); also private station land

blocked.name: H2 Hinde Tree
blocked.verify_notes: Macadamia integrifolia at 'Colliston', 926 Gilston Road, Gilston, City of Gold Coast, Queensland. Qld Heritage Register, listed 14 Aug 2008. One of ~30 macadamias believed planted in the 1920s by Michael James Hinde on his farm established 1879; tagged in 1948 by the Department of Agriculture and Stock as the parent of one of two cultivars that seeded Australia's commercial macadamia industry. Living, good condition per the National Trust's own tree register (trusttrees.org.au), roughly 100 years old, trunk diameter ~1m, height ~8m. BLOCKED: the National Trust's own register lists public access as 'Restricted' for this specific tree, on what is private farm property. Confirms the note in the brief that this sits on private land under hard rule 10; no evidence found of any public viewing arrangement, booked tour or open day.
blocked.reason: private farm property, access explicitly listed as Restricted

blocked.name: The Robbers Tree
blocked.verify_notes: Heritage-listed Cypress Pine on a sand dune at the southern end of Stockyard Street, Cunnamulla, Shire of Paroo, Queensland (Qld Heritage Register, listed 21 Oct 1992). Site where bank robber Joseph Wells hid in the branches after an 1880 armed robbery, found only when a sheep dog sat barking beneath the tree. BLOCKED: DEAD. Multiple sources (Wikipedia, and consistent with Cunnamulla Tourism's own account) confirm the tree was struck by lightning in 2021 and damaged beyond repair; only the stump remains on Stockyard Street, with a permanent memorial planned for the site. The 1920s photo and plaque photo in the brief predate this. A stump/memorial site is not a living collectible entry.
blocked.reason: dead: struck by lightning 2021, damaged beyond repair, stump only remains

blocked.name: Fig Tree, Gladstone
blocked.verify_notes: Weeping fig (Ficus benjamina), corner of Roseberry and Auckland Streets, Gladstone Central, on the grounds of the Government Offices; planted c.1903 by local businessman James Friend. Qld Heritage Register, listed 3 Dec 2003; National Trust of Queensland Register of Significant Trees since 1983. Height 12m, canopy spread ~37m, trunk circumference 660cm. Alive and apparently in reasonable condition (saved by a community campaign in the early 1990s when it appeared to be declining; a 1993 sign records its history, a wooden seat sits beneath it). Publicly accessible: government office grounds, open street corner, overhangs a car park. Would pass evidence bar easily (age, girth, species, two sources). BLOCKED on the single-tree-destination test rather than on evidence: this would be its own place at 440.8km from the nearest published city, so it stands or falls alone. Found no tourism promotion beyond a local plaque and office-worker seating; it reads as a well-loved shade tree beside a car park rather than a reason to travel, and demand is the weakest in this batch (27 reads/month). Kept as a strong lead for data/leads in case a Gladstone-area page develops with other trees.
blocked.reason: fails single-tree-destination test: good local heritage tree but not a travel destination on its own; no tourism promotion found

blocked.name: Landsborough's Blazed Tree (Camp 69)
blocked.verify_notes: Coolibah (Eucalyptus coolabah) marked 16 May 1862 by William Landsborough's expedition ('V.+Q. EXPN / L.C.69 MAY 16 1862'), apparently carved onto a pre-existing Aboriginal scar. Near Bakers Bend, ~29km south of Charleville off the Mitchell Highway, Shire of Murweh (26.6761S 146.1580E). Qld Heritage Register #602715, listed 18 June 2009. Blaze described as extremely well preserved in 2015 photographs; tree appears alive in those photos (no report of death found). One of only two known surviving blazes from this expedition in the Charleville district. BLOCKED on access: Wikipedia's own text places it 'on a grazing leasehold of just under 684 hectares... off the Mitchell Highway near Bakers Bend', i.e. inside private pastoral leasehold land rather than in the highway's road reserve; no source found describing a public access arrangement, gate, or signposted pull-off. Per hard rule 10, when in doubt about whether the public can reach a tree without crossing private land, it is left out.
blocked.reason: on private grazing leasehold land, no evidence of public access from the highway

blocked.name: Landsborough's Blazed Tree (Camp 67)
blocked.verify_notes: Coolibah (Eucalyptus coolabah), blaze reading 'L.C.67 MAY 10 1862' with '+Q EXPN' above, marked on a levee beside a small creek feeding the Warrego River system, ~10km south of Charleville off the Mitchell Highway (26.4904S 146.1947E). Qld Heritage Register #602716, listed 18 June 2009, the sibling site to Camp 69 (~50km apart, same 1862 Landsborough expedition, correctly treated as a separate candidate here). Girth 3.7m at 1m above ground, canopy spread 13.5m. Blaze repainted for visibility. Alive per the source describing the current tree and its blaze in the present tense; no death report found. BLOCKED on access: explicitly described as sitting on private freehold property off the Mitchell Highway, with no indication of a public easement, pull-off or road-reserve location. Same reasoning as Camp 69: per hard rule 10, a tree reachable only by crossing private land without an access arrangement stays out.
blocked.reason: on private freehold land, no evidence of public access from the highway

blocked.name: Hodgkinson's Marked Tree
blocked.verify_notes: Coolibah (Eucalyptus microtheca) on the northeastern bank of Lake Mary, in the homestead paddock of Rocklands Station, near Camooweal, far western Queensland (19.8540S 138.1062E). Marked 27 Sept 1876 by explorer surveyor W.O. Hodgkinson (a broad arrow over 'H' over 'LXXXVIII' over the date), during a Queensland government expedition. Qld Heritage Register #600741, listed 21 Oct 1992. Checked and found healthy, still leaning over the lake, at Christmas 2003; markings visible in c.1983 photos and believed still visible, though no confirmation newer than 2003 was found. BLOCKED: sits in the homestead paddock of Rocklands Station, a private pastoral property, with access apparently only practical by boat up the Georgina River system; no visitor infrastructure, path or public access arrangement found anywhere. Fails hard rule 10 (private working station) and, independently, the single-tree-destination test: this is a remote station paddock reachable only by boat, 915km from the nearest published city, with nothing built for a visitor to use.
blocked.reason: private station homestead paddock, boat-only access, no public access arrangement
